newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Police fire teargas at supporters of Zaire premier.
newsitem.headline: Police fire teargas at supporters of Zaire premier.

text.p: Police in Zaire's capital fired teargas to halt a march on parliament by supporters of new Prime Minister Etienne Tshisekedi on Monday, witnesses said.
The protesters, trying to prevent parliament from meeting to remove Tshisekedi from office, continued their march undeterred. There were no immediate reports of casualties.
"There were about 1,000 demonstrators heading towards parliament. Police fired teargas but they kept going and were joined by more people," one witness said.
Another group of militant Tshisekedi followers gathered in the city's central boulevard and was heading for parliament, other witnesses said.

Tshisekedi, a radical politician and President Mobutu Sese Seko's chief political rival, was appointed last week but parliament has initiated moves to remove him because of his unilateral decision to dissolve the assembly.
The opposition bloc that returned Tshisekedi to the job he had been sacked from four years ago joined rivals on Saturday to try to oust the prime minister.
Parliament scheduled a session on Monday to start procedures that could lead to his removal.
Tshisekedi has particularly angered Mobutu's supporters, who dominate parliament, by completely excluding them from a cabinet he announced on Thursday, his first day in office.
The political turmoil sparked by Tshisekedi's actions has complicated Zaire's crisis as rebels advancing in the east and south look set to capture the country's second city Lubumbashi.

Rebels now hold more than a third of the vast nation since taking up arms last october. There is no sign of a beakthrough in the first direct talks between the warring parties, which began in South Africa on Saturday.
